answers.core: Since it's a core feature in gdscript, it should also be one in C#.
answers.workaround:
3 possible workarounds:
1. Do not use categories in C#. That's what I'm doing now, I just add the properties in a reasonable order just as I would add them to the categories.
2. Use categories and the `[Export]` attribute and accepting that all variables will show up twice in the editor. Their values update accordingly, ie. changing one also changes the other so technically this is fine. But it bloats the inspector and is not a good workaround in my opinion.
3. Implement the class either in gdscript (losing all of C# type safety because properties from gdscript need to be accessed via `Get()` and `Set()`) or maybe even in C++ (not sure about that because I haven't yet used it in Godot)

title: In C# we cannot both add a property to category and have a default value
